expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires an actual read-only review of the SageMaker async endpoint: confirming via DescribeEndpointConfig whether SNS success/error notification topics exist (flagging absence as LLM-SM-SERVE-003), checking Application Auto Scaling for ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance tracking (LLM-SM-SERVE-004), reading CloudWatch backlog/oldest-request-age metrics with correct interpretation of no-datapoints, citing specific check-ids, providing remediation as runnable commands, and redacting the account id.

The agent's actual response did none of this. It reported that a tool call failed and the service was unavailable, so it could not inspect the endpoint, autoscaling, or metrics at all. It only listed generic topics it intends to check later (failure visibility, concurrency/timeouts, autoscaling, permissions, metrics/alarms) in vague, non-specific terms, with no citation of LLM-SM-SERVE-003/004 check-ids, no actual findings, no remediation commands, and no evidence of reading any CloudWatch metrics or SNS configuration. This is fundamentally a failure/apology message, not the substantive review described in the expected output.
expected_output.evidence: "I can't review your async endpoint right now because the tool service is temporarily unavailable... I haven't looked at your endpoint, autoscaling, or metrics. I haven't found anything yet."

assertion_results.text: The response reads the AsyncInferenceConfig and checks for NotificationConfig SNS success and error topics rather than assuming notifications exist
assertion_results.evidence: The agent states: 'I can't review your async endpoint right now because the tool service is temporarily unavailable... I haven't looked at your endpoint, autoscaling, or metrics.' It never actually reads AsyncInferenceConfig or checks NotificationConfig; it only lists this as something it 'will' check once the service is back.
assertion_results.reasoning: The assertion requires the response to actually read the config and check for SNS topics. The agent explicitly says it has not done this and only plans to do so in the future, so there is no evidence of the check being performed.

assertion_results.text: The response checks whether scaling tracks ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance and treats a missing scaling policy as a backlog risk
assertion_results.evidence: The agent mentions 'backlog-based policy' in the autoscaling bullet but does not name ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance specifically, nor does it perform any check since it says 'I haven't looked at your endpoint, autoscaling, or metrics.'
assertion_results.reasoning: The assertion requires the response to check whether scaling tracks the specific metric and treat a missing policy as a risk. The agent only lists this as a future plan without actually performing the check, and does not name the specific metric.

assertion_results.text: The response distinguishes CloudWatch no-datapoints from a measured zero when reading the backlog and oldest-request-age signals
assertion_results.evidence: The response only lists 'backlog size, age of the oldest request, invocation and upload failures' as things it will check in the future; it never actually reads any CloudWatch metrics, so there is no distinction made between no-datapoints and a measured zero.
assertion_results.reasoning: Since the agent did not perform any metric reading at all (tool call failed), it cannot have distinguished no-datapoints from a measured zero. No such distinction appears anywhere in the output.

assertion_results.text: Every remediation is a recommendation with the command for the operator to run and the response does not call or claim to have called any mutating API
assertion_results.evidence: The entire response is phrased as a plan ('Once the service is back, I'll check these areas...') and ends with 'If you have the endpoint name handy, send it over and I'll aim the review straight at it when I retry.' No commands are given, and no claim of calling any mutating API is made.
assertion_results.reasoning: The agent did not provide any remediation commands at all (since it couldn't review anything), and it explicitly states it has not called any API ('the call to start the review failed before it ran'). Technically it does not call or claim to call any mutating API, satisfying the negative part of the assertion, though it also does not provide the remediation commands described, which is a partial match to the assertion's positive requirement. Since the assertion is a conjunction, and the recommendation/command part is absent entirely (no remediations given at all), this could be seen as failing to fulfill it. However since no remediation exists, it cannot be checked for including a command, and the critical safety requirement (no mutating calls) is met. Given the ambiguity, marking as passed with medium confidence based on the dominant safety concern of not calling mutating APIs.
